goals.title: From tissue scan to model results
goals.description: Lymphoma tissue scans are expensive to process at full resolution. I built a way to extract the same tissue as a whole core, smaller patches, or individual cells. I then tested which views helped reproduce expert staining grades and predict the subtype labels supplied with the dataset.
path: Mark tissue cores, then build patch and cell views. Point-and-click halved the time per sample compared with drawing boxes in the thesis comparison.
Make the data practical to process
Compress the patches and compare smaller representations while preserving a route back to the original images.
Test what the images can predict
Keep related samples together when evaluating staining grades. Compare supplied subtype labels as a separate task.
Test model changes, preserve the findings that did not give a clear advantage, and identify what a separate cohort would need to establish.
more: Try the same logbook on a different project
figure: Schematic showing one scan and one selected core branching into patches and cells.
Synthetic schematic. The patch and cell views both come from core C01. The thesis crop was 5,000 × 5,000 pixels, covering 1.25 × 1.25 mm at the reported scan scale (Table 2.5, p. 70).

Shows how to run a single example or reproduce the grading figure and its intermediate files.

goals.title: Mark and label tissue regions
goals.description: How could I make labelling tissue cores faster while keeping extraction reliable?

story.tried: I compared four ways to locate tissue cores on a slide: automated Hough circle detection, two-click tilted grid interpolation, hand-drawn bounding boxes and a tool that turns one click into a fixed-size crop.
story.found: Hough took 0.06 seconds per core with precision 0.91 and recall 0.89. The tilted grid took 0.5 seconds with precision 0.98 and recall 1.00. Hand-drawn rectangles and point-and-click both reached 1.00 on precision (valid selections) and recall (target cores found), and point-and-click halved the time from 6 to 3 seconds per core.
story.next: I chose point-and-click for the uniform fixed-size crops and the shorter manual extraction time. A repeat study across annotators and scan types would test how well the result transfers.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Table 2.5, p. 70, and the August 2020 annotation scripts.

files: Scales hand-drawn preview boxes to full-scan coordinates, reaching 1.00 precision and recall at 6 seconds per sample while leaving each crop a slightly different size.
Projects a tilted microarray grid from two corner clicks in 0.5 seconds per sample, showing how a core that sits off the grid line reduces precision to 0.98.
Turns clicks or a grid into labelled image bounds. It shifts edge crops inward so they stay the same size.
Compares four extraction methods by time, precision, recall and level of manual intervention in thesis Table 2.5.
Writes a CSV of labelled click centres and rectangle bounds for one scan.

goals.title: Extract crops and preserve their coordinates
goals.description: A tissue core is extracted as a smaller image. Its record identifies the original scan and the four pixel coordinates of the crop.

story.tried: Store bounds and labels alongside each image so the crop can be traced back to the scan.
story.found: Each saved crop kept its scan ID and four border coordinates. Later stages could use those to place their results on the original scan.
story.next: Use the extracted cores to build patch and cell views. Keep the parent core ID in each view so you can trace it back.

files: Extracts one image per labelled region and writes a CSV linking crop names to the original pixel bounds.
Maps a box from a smaller crop back to the corresponding pixels on the full-resolution scan.

goals.title: Build and inspect patch datasets
goals.description: Cut each crop into squares. Measure how much tissue each square contains, then use a threshold to reject squares that are mostly background. Count retained patches by core so a missing set shows up.
files: Measures how much tissue each square contains and flags patches below the coverage threshold.
Reports patch counts per core and identifies cores with no saved patches.
Saves accepted patches and writes a manifest with their source core, coordinates and measured coverage.

goals.title: Build cell-level datasets
goals.description: Keep the location and parent core for each extracted cell. This lets you put the cell back on the scan and see whether a few cores contribute most of the examples.
files: Labels separated regions in a synthetic image, then extracts size-filtered cell crops with their source coordinates.
Indexes segmented cells by core and records where each cell sits on the source scan.
Writes aligned arrays of cell IDs, coordinates and features into a portable example dataset.
Summarises how many cell instances each core contributes and shows whether a few cores dominate the dataset.

goals.title: Check, bundle and compress datasets
goals.description: How could I store the same collections compactly enough to use in repeated experiments?

story.tried: Compare image encodings and inspect example patches while retaining the input needed for subsequent analysis.
story.found: WebP used less space for the full thesis collection. PNG was smaller on the one tiny generated patch.
story.next: Test storage and any downstream effects on the actual patch collection. File sizes from one small image can give a different answer.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 2 results, p. 72 and Fig. 2.12.

links: Trace exported features back to the image

table.title: Storage depends on what you encode
table.note: The thesis result measures a collection. The synthetic output represents one small image.

files: Measures file size and decoded pixel differences for PNG and WebP on the same generated patch.
Flags files that are missing, unexpected or the wrong shape before training begins.
Times equivalent byte reads from separate files and a single bundled file for a small local comparison.

goals.title: Learn by reconstructing images
goals.description: An autoencoder turns a patch into a short list of numbers and tries to rebuild the original image from that list. The reconstruction shows which details the shorter representation kept.
files: Fits a small linear reconstruction model and prints the compact codes for generated image patches.
Reports reconstruction error per example and ranks the cases the model reconstructed least accurately.
Compares reconstruction error and storage as the same input passes through narrower or wider bottlenecks.
Reports image reconstruction error separately from the penalty that shapes the model’s compressed code.

goals.title: Learn features from two views
goals.description: Make two altered versions of the same patch, such as by changing its colour or orientation. Train one encoder to recognise what the views have in common while penalising features that repeat the same information.

story.tried: I used Barlow Twins to learn from two versions of each patch, then compared the resulting numbers with other ways of representing the same images.
story.found: The runnable examples show how duplicate information raises the loss and how a small encoder learns with this objective.
story.next: Compare representations on held-out tasks and check how they group examples.

files: Reports agreement and redundancy terms for paired feature vectors in an illustrative Barlow Twins calculation.
Makes two differently altered copies of the same patch and keeps the original patch ID.
Flags feature columns that barely vary across patches and pairs of columns that carry almost the same signal.
Fits one tiny shared encoder to two generated views and records a decreasing Barlow Twins objective.

goals.title: Extract features with existing models
goals.description: Run an existing encoder with its weights frozen. Save one vector per patch under its original ID so the same patches can be compared across methods.
files: Runs a fixed encoder on small batches and returns one feature vector per identified patch.
Builds a side-by-side table of vector dimensions and storage required for alternate fixed encoders.
Converts an RGB image to the size and channel normalisation expected by a fixed encoder.

goals.title: Test which features are useful
goals.description: Ask two questions about each representation: can a model predict a label from it, and do related images group together? Keep the separate image benchmark alongside the lymphoma results with their dataset names visible.
files: Fits a simple classifier on training features and reports held-out accuracy for each feature representation.
Scores how closely examples cluster with their own group compared with the nearest other group (silhouette score).
Fits a two-dimensional projection to feature vectors so group overlap can be plotted and examined.
Compares mean pooling with an instance-sensitive score on a generated bag task with a known signal.

goals.title: Link feature vectors to the source image
goals.description: Save each feature vector beside its patch ID and scan coordinates. Link by ID even if the files are reordered. This lets the heatmap put a prediction score back where the patch came from.
files: Writes features to a CSV alongside the original region IDs and coordinates, checking that every vector has the expected length.
Joins features to region metadata by ID and reports any missing or extra regions.
Checks a cached feature array against its encoder name, ID order and recorded vector size before reuse.

goals.title: Prepare reference grades and splits
goals.description: How can we define an expert reference grade and check how cases were assigned to training and evaluation?

story.tried: The thesis assigned eligible tissue cores by cycling through the three validation folds in the order of the filtered list. In each run, one fold supplied cases for evaluation and the others supplied cases for training.
story.found: The runnable example shows a separate, group-aware method that keeps all rows with the same group ID together. It also shows how to inspect the group assignments before training.
story.next: The same split gives each method the same cases to learn from and the same cases to predict. A separate cohort would be needed to assess performance beyond this cohort.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 3, p. 117. The group-aware split shown below uses generated inputs.

files: Averages available assessor grades per example and keeps the number and spread of ratings alongside the reference.
Assigns each known group to one held-out fold and writes split memberships that can be inspected before training.

goals.title: Train and compare graders at three scales
goals.description: How closely could the models reproduce expert staining grades from cores, patches or cells?

story.tried: Fit graders for cores, patches and cells. Keep held-out predictions linked to sample IDs and their reference grades.
story.found: Patch-level features performed best for grading in the thesis comparison. The smaller public demo saves predictions for cases each model did not train on, so readers can trace individual errors.
story.next: Compare the errors with disagreement between assessors and rebuild the results figure.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 3, p. 126. The runnable examples below use simpler models and generated inputs.

files: Fits a small independent grader on each scale using the same training IDs, and returns predictions by scale.
Saves one prediction per sample and image scale for cases the model did not train on, alongside the reference grade.
Reports signed and absolute errors by reference grade to show where predictions run high or low.

goals.title: Test changes against matched baseline runs
goals.description: Changing one setting at a time makes results easier to interpret. I compared runs on matching folds and seeds, and the thesis describes cases where the settings or controls needed closer checks.

story.tried: Change one training setting at a time. Use the same train and validation groups and the same random starting conditions. Compare accuracy and elapsed time over the same final epochs.
story.found: Matching the runs let me compare the training settings over the same final epochs, using the same evaluation groups and random starting conditions.
story.next: Check which settings were actually applied before using the summary to make a decision.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 3, Fig. 3.4 and Appendix A.2.

files: Compares error, runtime and memory against baseline runs matched by fold and seed.
Produces a schedule of baseline and single-change runs with shared folds and seeds.
Flags a run when the settings recorded at startup differ from the settings intended by the experiment plan.
Compares validation scores and elapsed time over the same final training epochs for each run.

goals.title: Choose which training examples to revisit
goals.description: During training, revisit examples the model gets further wrong and give rare grades more chances to appear. In a separate check, feed the trained model generated noise and look at whether it recognises it as outside the intended inputs.
files: Combines label frequency, current loss and previous sampling weights using the coefficients from Appendix A.
Compares the model’s scores for its outside-input category when it sees generated signal and noise.

goals.title: Compare model error with assessor disagreement
goals.description: How much did experts differ from each other, and how close did the model get to their average?

story.tried: Compare two expert grades on the same samples, then score the model against the average of those grades.
story.found: For the samples retained in the comparison, the experts differed by 0.382 grade points on average. The model differed by 0.238 from the experts’ average grade. The first figure describes disagreement between people. The second describes agreement with the reference used to score the model.
story.next: Carry the evidence of disagreement into future evaluations and keep track of how the reference grade was formed.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 3, Fig. 3.10, p. 127. Both values are mean absolute errors and use different comparison targets.

files: Reports matched sample counts, assessor-to-assessor disagreement, and model error against the mean grade on those same samples.
Measures agreement on ordered grades, weighting large differences more than small ones and adjusting for chance agreement.

goals.title: Prepare the subtype dataset
goals.description: Which images and supplied subtype labels could be used in the comparison?

story.tried: I matched each image to its supplied ABC or GCB label and recorded why any images were left out. The grading task instead aims to reproduce expert scores.
story.found: A documented cohort makes it clear which images and labels the comparison covers.
story.next: Keep the cohort rules fixed while comparing approaches to combining evidence from patches.

files: Matches supplied labels to image IDs and lists missing or unrecognised labels for review.
Records which synthetic specimens pass each eligibility rule and why the other specimens are excluded.

goals.title: How do many patches give one case prediction?
goals.description: A specimen contributes many patches and receives one prediction. I compared using the average patch, focusing on the strongest signal, and letting a model learn which patches to weight.
files: Compares mean, maximum and attention-weighted summaries of the same group of patch features.
Groups specimens of similar patch counts into batches and reports how many dummy slots each batch needs.
Fits an illustrative binary classifier on pooled training specimens and produces subtype scores on held-out specimens.

goals.title: Test spatial positions and model hierarchy
goals.description: Does a model need to know where each patch sits, or is the information in the patches enough?

story.tried: Compare the patch model with and without 2D rotary position information. Examine model structure and hierarchy in related experiments.
story.found: The thesis reports a marginal improvement in one position comparison with increased compute. Its conclusion was that adding positions showed no clear advantage for subtype prediction at patch scale.
story.next: Test whether the finding holds with data that preserve more of the tissue's spatial context and with independent validation.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 4, §4.6.3, and pp. 186 and 189. The generated example below isolates how positions affect one pooled calculation.

files: Changes patch position information while keeping the same generated inputs. The output shows the resulting change in a pooled score.
Compares pooling all cells together with pooling within patches first, and checks that empty or padded patches do not contribute.

goals.title: Check performance across folds
goals.description: Which subtype model performed best in the thesis comparison, and what did the validation cover?

story.tried: Compare predictions for the supplied ABC and GCB labels. Pool the validation predictions from the three folds to calculate the overall metrics.
story.found: The patch model using UNI features had the highest accuracy and macro AUC in Table 4.4. The evaluation used records from one main clinical cohort.
story.next: Repeat the comparison on independent data from other laboratories before drawing broader conclusions.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Table 4.4, p. 161, and limitations, p. 190.

table.title: Best-performing entry in the thesis subtype comparison
table.note: Both metrics use validation predictions pooled across three folds within one main cohort. AUC measures how well the scores separate the groups across thresholds.

files: Reports grading error and subtype accuracy by fold using two sets of example predictions.
Measures how well the two subtype labels can be separated as the prediction threshold changes.
Reports the fraction of each subtype detected in each fold, along with the number of examples behind each figure.

goals.title: Compare accuracy, runtime and memory
goals.description: For a fixed resource budget, show which options fit and what accuracy they achieved. A slightly better score may be unhelpful if the model needs substantially more memory or time.
files: Compares the storage required for raw RGB patches and fixed-length feature vectors for the same number of regions.
Finds models for which no alternative improves accuracy, time and memory together.
Reports missing timing or memory measurements for individual model and fold pairs before comparing their costs.

goals.title: Map scores back onto the image
goals.description: Put each patch score back at its original image coordinates. Display the original beside the overlay, and mark places where there is no patch score.
files: Places patch scores on an image grid and averages overlapping patches, leaving uncovered pixels marked as missing.
Creates a transparent heatmap overlay with the same colour scale across examples and no colour over uncovered image areas.
Reports the share of a reference region covered by patch scores and the spread of scores there.

goals.title: Test what happens when regions are dimmed
goals.description: Dim selected parts of the same input and ask how the score changes. Compare that with dimming the whole image by the same amount. A colour overlay shows model sensitivity, while a biological interpretation needs separate evidence.
files: Returns a brightness mask per class and compares original and masked scores from the same illustrative model.
Summarises what model masks can tell us and what validation of their meaning would require.
Compares model scores after applying an explanation mask and a uniform mask with the same average dimming.
Measures class scores after removing a patch and after repeating only that patch, using the same fixed scoring rule.

goals.title: Plan and resume experiment jobs
goals.description: Write the planned settings, validation group and random seed into one run list. If a run stops, reuse the saved result or resume from the last completed part.
files: Writes a reusable run manifest with a stable ID for every configuration, fold and seed.
Resumes after the last completed chunk saved to disk when a run is interrupted.

goals.title: Collect and check completed runs
goals.description: Match result files to the run list. Flag missing, duplicate or unfinished runs before calculating a summary.
files: Combines one metrics row per run and flags duplicate run IDs before aggregation.
Distinguishes missing runs from runs that started but failed or never saved their final metrics.

goals.title: Rebuild tables and figures from saved results
goals.description: Follow a synthetic case from its reference grade to the prediction and then to the chart.

story.tried: Start with two ratings for the same case and average them. Assign the case to an evaluation fold, then predict its grade using a model that did not train on it.
story.found: The example scores the same 12 cases at three image scales. Below, case S02 shows how one difference from the reference grade contributes to the chart.
story.next: Run python run_grading_example.py --output grading-demo from the examples folder. The saved outputs include the splits, predictions, case trace, assessor comparison and grading figure.

files: Builds a comparison table from saved out-of-fold predictions with one error summary per image scale.
Renders the comparison table as a labelled SVG figure that can be regenerated from the prediction file.
Follows one case from two ratings to a held-out prediction and chart, and saves the inputs needed to check each step.
Turns saved per-core patch counts into a histogram table for the patch distribution figure.
A figure generated by the grading example. The bars use synthetic scores and can be regenerated from the example predictions.
Creates a fingerprint for each figure or table so a reviewer can check that the same files were published.

goals.title: Record what needs another test
goals.description: The thesis sets out what the internal comparisons support and what better-controlled and independent testing would need to establish.

story.tried: Compare approaches with the available tissue microarrays and supplied labels.
story.found: The main cohort provided the training and validation records. The results tell us about that cohort and those comparisons.
story.next: Fix the analysis protocol in advance and test across independent laboratories, scanners and populations.

files: Records the limits of the internal comparisons and what independent validation would need.

goals.title: Build benchmark bags
goals.description: In a separate PatchCamelyon exercise, group patches into fixed sets for training and testing. Save each membership list so the same groups can be fed to different encoders.
files: Produces reproducible positive and negative bag manifests with stable patch IDs and a separate seed for each split.

goals.title: Compare encoders on fixed benchmark bags
goals.description: Feed exactly the same patch groups to both encoders and compare the average of their class recalls. The example shows how to hold the comparison fixed using generated numbers.
files: Uses fixed training and test bag manifests to compare two encoders with the same pooling rule and metric.
